clue.text: Support on course drops internally for student

indicators.note: internally tells us one piece sits inside the other, here the drops inside the support

parts.note: a golf tee supports the ball on the course
drops of water are rain

explanation.surface: A golfer's tee leaks on the course, an odd thing for a student to notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internally' puts RAIN inside TEE, splitting it T...EE. A golf tee is the peg holding the ball at the start of each hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is someone learning a job, a type of student or apprentice.

clue.text: One may type a note to member

parts.note: te is a note in the sol-fa scale
MP is Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone types a memo addressed to an MP.
explanation.walkthrough: TE (also spelt ti) is the seventh note of the do-re-mi scale.
explanation.definitionFit: A temp is a temporary office worker, often a typist.

clue.text: Try one real agent wrongfully as top US lawman

indicators.note: wrongfully suggests the letters are put together in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Putting a genuine agent on trial unjustly would be a scandal for the chief legal officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The US Attorney General heads the Department of Justice, the country's chief law officer.

clue.text: Bird's head appearing above tile on church

indicators.note: appearing above says the first piece sits higher in this down answer
on means placed on top of the next piece in a down entry

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
tile is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A bird pokes its head above the tiles on a church roof.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small songbird that climbs tree trunks head first.

clue.text: Situation involving Artie, Grant and Ellen?

indicators.note: involving suggests the names are entangled together, their letters mixed up

explanation.surface: Three named people, Artie, Grant and Ellen, caught up in a romantic tangle.
explanation.walkthrough: The three names are rearranged; and three people romantically entangled are themselves an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a love situation in which three people are involved, such as a married couple and a lover.

clue.text: Harmful black drink almost drunk

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
ale is a drink, a type of beer

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its final letter, stopping just short

parts.note: full is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A dark beer nearly finished, and the drinker already the worse for wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last letter from FULL, giving FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Baleful means menacing or destructive, a near synonym of harmful.

clue.text: Over-the-top article that puts a stop to barefaced cheek?

definitions.text: Over-the-top article that puts a stop to barefaced cheek?

parts.words: Over-the-top article that puts a stop to barefaced cheek?
parts.note: over-the-top means worn over the head, and the garment covers the bare face and cheeks

explanation.walkthrough: Over-the-top usually means excessive, but here a woollen head covering goes over the top of the head and hides the bare cheeks; it is named after a Crimean War battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted hood covering head and face, leaving only the eyes, stops the cheeks being bare.

clue.text: Longing to be on river at East Sheen

parts.note: lust is strong longing

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to be on the Thames at East Sheen, a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: East Sheen is a district of south-west London, so 'Sheen' looks like part of a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is a soft glow or gloss on a surface, a sheen.

clue.text: Gossip's lie about large man coming to premature end on gallows

indicators.note: about tells us the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: a fib is a small lie

indicators.note: premature end means the word is cut short of its final letter

parts.note: Bertie is a man's name
a gibbet is a gallows

explanation.surface: Gossip has it that a big man died before his time on the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L into FIB to make FLIB; 'coming to premature end' trims BERTIE to BERTI.
explanation.definitionFit: A flibbertigibbet is a frivolous, flighty person who chatters endlessly, a gossip.

clue.text: One criticised after support for enacted laws

indicators.note: after places the following words later in the answer than the support

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
I is the Roman numeral one
slated means harshly criticised

explanation.surface: One politician is slated after backing a bill that made it into law.
explanation.definitionFit: To have legislated is to have made or passed laws.

clue.text: Religious music, a tiny bit, set before tenor

indicators.note: set before says the first piece comes ahead of the second in the answer

parts.note: a mote is a speck, a tiny bit of dust
T is a standard abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: Church music in which a scrap of melody is set ahead of the tenor line.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short choral composition, usually sacred, sung in church services.

clue.text: Joining up middle of tent by leaning over

indicators.note: middle of asks for the central letters of the word that follows

parts.note: a ship listing is leaning over to one side

explanation.surface: Someone joins a camp by bending over the middle of a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of TENT is EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlisting is signing up, especially for the armed forces.

clue.text: In particular, Magna Carta reveals this spirit

indicators.note: reveals says the answer is shown openly within the clue's own words

explanation.surface: A historian claims the great charter discloses a favourite brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across particulAR MAGNA Carta.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagnac is a brandy from Gascony in France, a spirit distilled from wine.

clue.text: Puzzle using picturesque wordplay?

parts.note: describes a puzzle in which pictures and symbols stand for words or syllables

explanation.definitionFit: A rebus represents words with pictures, a form of visual riddle.

clue.text: Frets at tea-somehow it lingers on the tongue

indicators.note: somehow signals the letters are arranged in some other order

explanation.surface: Someone worries over tea because something unpleasant stays in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftertaste is a flavour that stays in the mouth after eating or drinking.

clue.text: Something long and narrow found on the continental shelf?

definitions.text: Something long and narrow found on the continental shelf?

parts.words: Something long and narrow found on the continental shelf?
parts.note: the continental shelf sounds geological, but means a European baker's shelf holding a long thin bread

explanation.walkthrough: 'continental shelf' is the seabed off a coast; here it is a bakery shelf with a baguette-style loaf on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A long slender bread loaf from France is long and narrow and sits on a baker's shelf.

clue.text: Region in Far East

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A region somewhere in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across fAR EAst.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a zone or district, the same as a region.

clue.text: State: "OK"

parts.note: OK is read not as approval but as the postal code of a US state, which is also a famous musical title

explanation.walkthrough: OK is the standard two-letter US postal abbreviation for this state.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma is the US state whose postal abbreviation is OK.

clue.text: Keenness that's an advantage

explanation.surface: An eagerness that gives one the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sharpness or keenness, and also a competitive advantage, as in having the edge over rivals.

clue.text: What might be baked in fire I cut

definitions.text: What might be baked in fire I cut

parts.words: What might be baked in fire I cut
parts.note: the speaker is a kitchen blade that slices what comes out of the oven

explanation.walkthrough: Read it as the tool speaking: 'What might be baked in fire, I cut'.
explanation.definitionFit: A serrated kitchen blade is used to slice loaves that have been baked in an oven.

clue.text: Annoy ancient hero

explanation.surface: Pestering an old legendary warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to bully or harass; Hector was the Trojan champion in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Present perhaps causing strain

explanation.surface: A gift that brings on stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Present is one grammatical tense of a verb; tense also means taut or stressful, causing strain.

clue.text: A very emotional moment, to start with a song and a prayer

indicators.note: to start with asks for the opening letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A deeply moving moment, opening with a solo, then a hymn of devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ave Maria, or Hail Mary, is a Catholic prayer to the Virgin, often set to music.

clue.text: Sheep on river vessel

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A sheep stands by the river beside a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug, a vessel for water.

clue.text: Plan to bring back excellent pastries

indicators.note: bring back tells us the combined pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: mega is slang for excellent
tarts are pastries

explanation.surface: A scheme to return some top-notch pastries to the bakery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring back' turns MEGATARTS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a scheme or ruse, a cunning plan.

clue.text: Bend on river where helmsman's losing head with rower

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a cox steers a rowing boat, the helmsman
the bow is the rower seated nearest the front of the boat

explanation.surface: On a river bend the coxswain is distracted while rowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' takes C from COX, leaving OX.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxbow is a U-shaped meander in a river, which may become a lake.

clue.text: Spread out, in general, when disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of the word are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A general spreads out his troops once he is disturbed.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge is to expand or make bigger, to spread out.

clue.text: He betrays characteristic macho demeanour in the end

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic feature

indicators.note: in the end asks for the final letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A turncoat gives himself away by his macho manner in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor is someone who betrays country or friends.
